**2. Resolution source.** No specific source is named. In practice it is the club's official statements (realmadrid.com) and major media. Real Madrid's site currently lists "Mourinho's side" and "Mourinho's men". Wikipedia's season page and La Liga's team list show him as head coach. I found no announcement of any departure.

  - The 2025–26 season already had two changes: Xabi Alonso left and Arbeloa replaced him (SI), so the club is not shy about changing manager.
- Mourinho's own history: he has not lasted beyond about 2–3 years at recent clubs. Fenerbahçe let him go after a year, and he left Benfica after a year. He also left Chelsea (Dec 2007 and Dec 2015) and Man United (Dec 2018) mid-season, but only after poor results.

The question names no specific source. Resolution depends on credible reporting of intentional destruction of more than a de minimis part of the structure. Nothing like that has been reported as of today.

## Web research
**Briefing: OpenRouter weekly tokens, Dec 21–27, 2026 bar**

**1. Current status (as of Nov 22, 2026)**
- The question is undecided. The Dec 21 bar is a month away.
- Recent weekly totals, which are mostly secondhand:
  - Week of Oct 26: about 194T. Menlo's Deedy Das charted it on Nov 2, and several outlets repeated it. OpenRouter processed approximately 194 trillion tokens in the week ending October 26, 2026.
  - Week of Nov 9: 199T had been processed at the time of the snapshot, with the week on pace for about 213T. Treat that as a mid-week projection. One HN commenter says these projections are often wrong.
  - Week of Nov 16: I found no confirmed total. Kalshi says traders heavily favor token use for Nov 16 to 22 coming in above 224T tokens. The market also lists higher thresholds (325T, 330T, 335T), but I couldn't see their prices.
- Growth rate: Deedy Das said volume doubles every 10.5 weeks. Polymarket's blurb repeats this as "doubling roughly every 10 weeks". The 10.5-week figure is an investor claim, and I found no OpenRouter announcement stating it.
- Earlier benchmarks:
  - Mid-May 2026: about 25T/week at the Series B.
  - Week of May 18–24: 28.9T.
  - Mid-2026: weekly usage had passed 90T by one report (CryptoBriefing). This conflicts with the roughly 29T figures for May and June, so treat the 90T number with caution.
  - Late October: about 194T.
- Model-level data (the rankings page, about Nov 21):
  - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is #1 at 63.3T (+15%).
  - The other top-10 models are well below that (second place is 15.3T).
  - The top 10 sum to roughly 128T, so the total is well above that.
  - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 alone went from 45.5T (week of Oct 24–30) to 59.2–61.2T (week through Nov 16) to 63.3T.
- Concentration risk: DeepSeek has capped free service usage for the first time amid a compute shortage (BigGo, about Nov 19). Pandaily reports users seeing daily caps and shorter inputs. This could dent the largest single model's volume.
- Composition: agent traffic is about 80% of tokens. OpenRouter's head of insights posted that agent tokens are up 106x since the first week of January and human tokens up 7x (Nov 16).

**2. Resolution source**
The rankings page (openrouter.ai/rankings#top-models) currently shows the weekly top-model table and chart. The resolution figure is the Dec 21 bar's displayed total. I could not retrieve the chart's total-bar values directly. OpenRouter also has a daily/weekly token-totals dataset API that matches the rankings chart (prompt plus completion tokens).

**3. Base rate and trajectory**
- Weekly volume milestones: 10B (Jan 2024), 100B (Sep 2024), 1T (Mar 2025), 10T (Feb 2026), 194T (late Oct 2026). Growth has been steep and mostly monotonic.
- Recent week-over-week growth is slower than the doubling claim implies. Going from about 194T (Oct 26) to about 213T (Nov 9) is roughly 10% in two weeks. A 10.5-week doubling would be roughly 7% per week.
- Plateau signals:
  - An HN thread titled "Token-maxxing is dead, OpenRouter's token usage plateaus" (about 34 days ago, so around Oct 19) noted weeks that were flat or slightly down.
  - A commenter pointed out that similar plateaus happened before, for example at the end of July.
- Holiday effect: I found no data on how the Christmas week affected OpenRouter volume in 2025. Holiday dips in developer usage are plausible. Agent-driven traffic (80%) may blunt them, but that is an inference, not something I found evidence for.

**4. Scheduled events and drivers before Dec 21**
I found no specific scheduled events. Factors that could move the number:
- New model releases and free-tier promotions. The recent surge was driven by DeepSeek's cheap Flash snapshots.
- DeepSeek capacity limits, and any pricing changes such as the off-peak versus peak pricing.
- OpenRouter's routing-engine changes.
- The Dec 21–27 Christmas and holiday lull.
- Any change to how the chart bins weeks. If bins moved off Monday–Sunday, the question would use the last full week of 2026.

**5. Markets and forecasters**
- Metaculus community estimate for this question: 282T, with a 220T–353T interval, as of the search snapshot.
- Kalshi (series KXTOKENUSE), Nov 16–22: heavily favors above 224T. It lists upper thresholds up to 335T, with prices not visible to me. A December-week market probably exists but I didn't find it.
- Polymarket:
  - The week of Nov 2 market resolved at "205T+" at 100%, with its lowest bucket at <175T. That points to a week at or above 205T.
  - An Oct 26–Nov 22 four-week market had 92.5% on 775T+ (as of about Oct 31).
  - Polymarket markets for the weeks of Nov 9 and Nov 16 also exist, but I couldn't see their prices.

**6. Strongest evidence on each side**
- Higher than about 280T:
  - Compounding has been strong.
  - Agent workloads keep growing.
  - Cheap Chinese flash models keep gaining share.
  - Kalshi lists thresholds as high as 335T for the Nov 16–22 week, which suggests some traders see a much higher run rate than 213T. I couldn't see the prices.
- Lower than about 280T:
  - Week-over-week growth in the observed totals (194T to about 213T) is below the doubling-rate claim.
  - A DeepSeek compute shortage and usage caps threaten the model that supplies about a third of tokens.
  - Holiday-week developer activity is likely to dip.
  - Traffic is concentrated in a few models, and some of it is free or promotional, which can reverse quickly.
  - Commenters question how much of the volume is system-prompt overhead from agent tools such as Hermes.

**Gaps:** I did not find the confirmed Nov 16–22 total, the Kalshi or Polymarket prices for December, or 2025 holiday-week data. Check the rankings chart or API dataset for the actual weekly totals for Nov 16 and Nov 23.

## Web research
**Briefing: How many bots will finish in the top 10 of the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026?**

  - Laertes and ManticAI finished 1st and 2nd, and FutureSearch finished 5th.

**2. Resolution source**
- The source is the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026 leaderboard, adjusted to count the top 10 bots and prize-eligible users together (the official board excludes bots). That question page is metaculus.com/questions/45619.
- The question page shows a community forecast of **5.1 bots (interquartile range 4–6)**, with 148 forecasters. Top key factors listed are "Elite bots consistently rank in top 10" and "New bots are already posting strong results".

- The Fall season is still open, so the leaderboard is still moving.

**3. Base rate / trend**
- Summer 2025: Mantic was 8th of 549, the first bot ever in the top 10 of the Cup series. That was 1 bot. In June 2025 the top bot (built by Metaculus) came 25th.
- Spring 2026: Two top-10 AIs (manticAI and Laertes) repeated their top-10 performance in summer. Preseen came third in the Spring 2026 Cup. I did not find a spring bot count in the top 10.
- Summer 2026: 5 bots in the top 10, both mid-season and at the end.
- Trend: 1 bot (Summer 2025) → at least 1–3 (Spring 2026) → 5 (Summer 2026). Bots improve at about 0.9 Metaculus Elo points per month (Scott Alexander citing Metaculus data).
- Season-to-season bot rank is noisy. Preseen-Chestnut was top-10 in spring but down to #40 in mid-summer.
- Caveats:
  - The Cup scoring rewards consistent updating and coverage, which favours bots.
  - In the controlled Spring 2026 FutureEval, 10 Pros beat the 10 best bots by 1.25 head-to-head points per question over 99 shared questions. The GitHub PR says the Pro lead narrowed and was not statistically significant.

**4. Scheduled events before resolution**
- Cup season closes **Jan 1, 2027**. Questions resolve after that, and this question resolves once all other questions have resolved. That may be after Jan 1, because some Cup questions may resolve late.
- The Fall 2026 FutureEval Bot Tournament (bot-only) runs Sep 28, 2026 to Jan 6, 2027. It is separate, but bot makers may reuse their bots in the Cup.
- Question resolutions through December will change scores. Late-resolving questions with large swings can reshuffle ranks.
- I did not find any rule changes for bots in the Fall Cup. I also did not find confirmation that laertes, manticAI, cassi, FutureSearch or Preseen are entered this season.

- The Metaculus community on this question: 5.1 (4–6).
- The bot forecast on 2026-09-21: 5.62.

- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market on this question.

**6. Strongest evidence on each side**
- Toward more bots (6 or more):
  - The 5/10 result in Summer 2026, including 1st and 2nd.
  - The steady improvement trend.
  - Bots won on coverage and updating, which the scoring favours.
  - Several independent bot teams (Mantic, laertes, cassi, FutureSearch, Preseen) are strong.
  - Mantic's $25M funding suggests continued investment.

question.title: Will Venezuela announce a presidential election before 2027?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: Will Venezuela announce a presidential election (with a specific date) before 2027?**

**1. Current status (as of 22 Nov 2026): not met. Outlook is leaning No.**
- **No date set.** No election date had been announced as of 18 November. The third round of government–opposition talks ended without an election timetable.
- **Rodríguez, 29 Oct.** The acting president promised "all the elections our Constitution mandates", run by a renewed electoral authority, but gave no date. She said the political horizon is not measured by a date on the calendar but by a sequence of objectives.
- **US roadmap (State Department briefing, 26–27 Oct; Rubio repeated it ~9 Nov).**
  - A new Supreme Court (TSJ) is targeted for mid-December, with a new electoral council (CNE) shortly after.
  - Rodríguez would then declare the presidency vacant, opening a six-month period to hold elections.
  - The CNE would then set the election date. The official could not give a concrete date, because the renewed CNE does not yet exist.
  - One analysis suggests that if the TSJ is installed in mid-December and the CNE in January, the vacancy declaration could come between late January and February 2027. That would be after the question deadline.
- **Legal authority.** Under the US plan, the date comes from the new CNE, which does not yet exist. That makes a date announcement before 1 Jan 2027 structurally unlikely. A unilateral announcement by Rodríguez or the National Assembly is possible but not signaled.
- **Timing of the election itself.** Opposition (Machado) wants 24 July 2027, while reports say Washington's plan points to 2028. A six-month window from a vacancy declared in early 2027 would put the vote in mid-to-late 2027, which fits the "before 1 Jan 2028" condition. The binding constraint is therefore whether a date is announced by 31 Dec 2026.

**2. Resolution source**
- No specific source is named. In practice it would be a CNE, National Assembly or Rodríguez announcement, or credible media reports of one. Right now none exists.
- Polymarket runs a related market, "Venezuela presidential election scheduled by…?", which closes ~1 Jan 2027. Its wording may differ from this question's, so check its rules.

**3. Base rate**
- I found no formal base rate. Historically, Venezuelan election dates have been set by the CNE, often on short notice and under government control: April 2013 (a few days after Chávez's death), April 2018 (announced Feb 2018), and July 2024 (announced March 2024).
- In this case, 10+ months have passed since Maduro's capture (Jan 2026) with no date.
- Polymarket's "by 31 Dec 2026" contract has drifted down over the year: ~49% earlier in the spring, 33% in April, 11–12% around early October, 18% a few weeks ago, 8.5% on 5 Nov, and 16.5% on 18 Nov.

**4. Scheduled or expected events before 31 Dec**
- **TSJ renewal.** The Assembly's final vote on the 32 magistrates, aimed at mid-December. A first reading of the TSJ law reform passed on 27 Aug. A new TSJ was also described as "by end of year".
- **CNE renewal.** Primero Justicia's roadmap has the five new CNE rectors designated in January–February 2027. That implies a late timeline.
- **Vacancy declaration by Rodríguez.** This is the trigger for the six-month clock. It is expected only after both the TSJ and CNE are renewed.
- Further dialogue rounds and opposition pressure. Opposition marches were held on 22/25 Oct. Machado, who returned to Venezuela on 26 Oct, said naming a new TSJ and CNE and setting the election date can be done "immediately", not necessarily in sequence.
- I did not find a specific scheduled date for a CNE or date announcement.

**5. Markets and forecasters (Polymarket, via Rio Times, 18 Nov 2026)**
- Election scheduled **by 31 Dec 2026: 16.5%**.
- By 31 Mar 2027: 29%, down from 39% on 8 Nov (one source reported 36.5% on 5 Nov).
- By Jun 2027: 52%. By Dec 2027: 70% (very thin volume).
- Total volume on the market is ~$670K, with thin liquidity.

**6. Strongest evidence on each side**

*Toward Yes:*
- The US is actively pushing a timeline and wants this done within Trump's term. Rubio said he intends to see this well before leaving his post.
- Rodríguez has publicly committed to elections and a renewed CNE. She is cooperating with Washington, which has heavy leverage over her government.
- TSJ renewal is targeted for mid-December. A fast sequence (TSJ, then CNE, then vacancy, then date) could theoretically all happen in December.
- Machado's return and public pressure are rising.

*Toward No:*
- The sequence has multiple steps, each prone to delay. The CNE, which sets the date, does not yet exist. The CNE reform lags the TSJ by weeks to months. The chavista-controlled Assembly must approve the magistrates.
- Rodríguez explicitly refuses to tie elections to a calendar date. Her 29 Oct speech gave no date.
- A State Department official said "You have to create the architecture for a credible election before you can actually call for one."
- Analysts flagged the risk that chavismo delays CNE reform.
- Reports suggest Washington's own plan may point to 2028 (unconfirmed). The market has drifted toward later dates.
- Only ~5.5 weeks remain, with no reported imminent announcement.

**Gaps:** I could not verify any news from 19–22 Nov. I did not find the Venezuelan constitutional text on the timing of a vacancy declaration. I could not confirm whether the Polymarket resolution wording matches this question (for example, a date versus "scheduling" in general).

slots.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 40 days, until December 31, 2026.

(b) **Status quo outcome:** No. No election date has been announced, and the body that would set it (a renewed CNE) does not yet exist.

(c) **No scenario:** The sequenced roadmap proceeds as described. The Assembly installs the new TSJ in mid-to-late December, possibly slipping. CNE rectors are named in January–February 2027, Rodríguez then declares the vacancy, and the new CNE sets a date in early 2027. Nothing date-specific is announced before the new year.

(d) **Yes scenario:** Under US and opposition pressure, a breakthrough in the dialogue compresses the sequence in December. Either the TSJ and CNE are appointed in quick succession and the CNE immediately announces a date (for example, July 2027), or Rodríguez or the National Assembly formally announces a specific date as part of a political agreement.

**Rationale:** Several things point strongly to No:

- **The sequence is long and has not started.** The US-backed roadmap runs TSJ, then CNE, then vacancy declaration, then a date set by the CNE. The first step is only targeted for mid-December, and analysts place the CNE renewal and vacancy declaration in January–February 2027.
- **Neither key actor is pushing for a date now.** Rodríguez explicitly refuses to tie elections to a calendar date. A State Department official said the architecture for a credible election must exist before one can be called.
- **Venezuelan political timelines slip.** Ten months have passed since Maduro's capture with no date, and the third round of talks ended without a timetable.
- **The question's bar is strict.** It needs a specific date announced by an entity with legal authority, not a general commitment or a roadmap.

The main path to Yes is a surprise political agreement that names a date, which Machado argues could be done "immediately". Polymarket's 16.5% for a related contract probably overstates this, given thin liquidity, longshot bias and possibly looser wording. I put the probability in the mid-single digits.

Probability: 5%

(a) Time left: about 5.5 weeks, until December 31, 2026.

(b) Status quo: No. No election date has been announced. The acting president refuses to tie elections to a calendar date, and the body expected to set the date, a renewed electoral council (CNE), does not yet exist.

(c) No scenario: The US-backed roadmap proceeds as described or slips. The new Supreme Court is seated in mid-to-late December, the new CNE is named in January or February 2027, Rodríguez then declares the presidency vacant, and the CNE sets a date in Q1 2027 or later. Nothing date-specific is announced before January 1.

(d) Yes scenario: Under strong US and opposition pressure after Machado's return, the dialogue produces a comprehensive agreement in December. Rodríguez, the National Assembly or a quickly reconstituted CNE then officially announces a specific 2027 date, such as July 24, 2027, before year-end.

Rationale: The published sequence puts the date announcement structurally after the deadline. question.title: What will be the highest intraday value of the VIX between October 1 and December 24, 2026?

## Web research
**Briefing: highest intraday ^VIX, Oct 1 – Dec 24, 2026 (as of Nov 22, 2026)**

**1. Current status**
- The question is undecided, because the window runs to Dec 24. The running maximum is already high.
- **Nov 20, 2026 (Friday):** ^VIX reached an intraday high of 40.03 and closed at 35.89. Yahoo shows previous close 28.44, open 28.63, day low 26.94, day high 40.03, and 52-week high 40.03. CNBC lists the 52-week high date as 11/20/26. The VIX added nine points Friday afternoon to briefly touch 40 as stocks extended a late-day drop.
- Earlier peaks this window:
  - **Oct 30:** Yahoo lists a high of 23.93 (open 18.43, close 19.42). Some outlets cite 22.31 for the same day. Yahoo's AU page also lists 22.31 as the Oct 16 high, so there is some inconsistency between sources.
  - **Nov 5:** the VIX closed at 28.18, up 69.7% from 16.61. One source puts the Nov 5 intraday high at 28.36, and others cite 28.09.
  - **Nov 19:** closed at 28.44, up 15.8%.
- Context for Nov 20:
  - The VIX was 16.34 at the end of September.
  - The Nov 20 high was above the March Iran-war peak, and the S&P 500 entered a correction.
  - The highest close in March 2026 was 31.05, on March 27.
- For the question to resolve higher than 40.03, the VIX has to trade above 40.03 on some day from Nov 23 to Dec 24 (about 22 trading days). Otherwise the answer is 40.03, per Yahoo.
- Possible data caveat: some secondary sources describe the Nov 20 high differently (30.04 premarket, "above 32" midday). The Yahoo and CNBC 40.03 figure is the final session high.

**2. Resolution source (Yahoo Finance ^VIX history)**
- Yahoo's quote page showed 35.89 (+26.20%) at the Nov 20 close, with a day high of 40.03.
- I could not retrieve the Yahoo history page row for Nov 20 directly. The 40.03 figure comes from the Yahoo quote page and CNBC.
- The history snippets I did find cover Oct 1–30. Their highest high is 23.93 on Oct 30.
- Yahoo's 52-week low was 13.38 (CNBC dates it Dec 24, 2025). The 2026 low was 14.21 in September.

**3. Base rate**
- Most quarters never see a VIX above 40. The 40.03 print was the highest since April 2025 (the tariff crisis).
- Reference points:
  - Record intraday high: 89.53 (Oct 24, 2008).
  - Record close: 82.69 (Mar 16, 2020). The all-time high is 82.69 per Macrotrends, and 89.53 is the intraday record per OptionsTradingIQ.
- The 2026 average through Nov 20 was 18.40, against 18.93 for 2025.
- The VIX is mean-reverting; it tends to spike in a day or two and then drift lower over weeks.
- This pattern held in November. The VIX eased from 28.18 on Nov 5 back to 17.49 by Nov 11, then rebounded to 35.89 by Nov 20.
- Since 1990, a VIX above 35 has doubled within a year only about 3% of the time. That is a mean-reversion statistic, not a probability of a new high.
- I did not find a statistic for how often a VIX that has just peaked near 40 makes a higher high within the next month. Historically, clusters like 2008, 2011, 2020 and 2025 sometimes made higher highs within weeks, but I did not verify this.

**4. Scheduled events before Dec 24**
- **Fed meeting, Dec 8–9.** Futures put a quarter-point hike near certainty. A half-point move was given about a 5% chance. Waller said on Nov 18 he backs a 50bp hike or much tougher guidance. The funds rate is 3.75–4.00%. The Fed Chair is Kevin Warsh.
- **PCE inflation report** in the week of Nov 23. This was flagged in a Nov 20 weekly wrap as the next data catalyst.
- **Dec 16 VIX/SPX expiry** (monthly options, third Friday is Dec 18; I did not verify the exact VIX expiration date).
- Other items:
  - Ongoing Nvidia news: the SEC accounting probe reported by Reuters, and the CEO exit.
  - AI-capex funding fears.
  - CTAs sold $57bn of equities over the prior month, and Goldman's Panic Index read 9 out of 10.
  - Possible oil or Iran headlines; an Oct 26 India VIX article mentioned crude and Saudi attack claims.
- Thanksgiving week (Nov 26 holiday, Nov 27 half-day) and year-end bring thinner liquidity.

**5. Forecasters and markets**
- **Metaculus**, the question's source. Snippets are of unclear date. One snapshot showed a community estimate of 24.9 (interquartile 22.6–28.1), which is stale because it is below the already-realized 40.03. Other snippets (149 and 173 days old) listed ">40". I could not see the current community forecast.
- Prediction markets:
  - A separate market on S&P 500 reaching 8,000 collapsed from 72% to 6%. I found no VIX-level market.
- Futures curve:
  - I did not find current VIX futures prices.
  - On Oct 26 the curve was in contango, but I found no data after the Nov 20 spike.

**6. Evidence on each side**

*Toward the answer being exactly 40.03 (no new high):*
- The VIX tends to mean-revert quickly. The Nov 5 spike halved in six days.
- 40.03 was reached late Friday as a brief print. Cboe's Mandy Xu called the move a mechanical reaction to the index slump and its effect on longer-dated options, not a rush for fresh downside protection.
- A Nov 18 relief rally followed Nvidia's earnings beat (revenue about $115.8bn).
- After past 50%+ one-day VIX spikes, the S&P 500 rose a month later nine times out of 10.
- Retail and institutional dip-buying has been reported. The Fed hike is already priced in.
- Commentators call the sell-off a buying opportunity (Yardeni).

*Toward a higher high:*
- Momentum is strong:
  - The S&P 500 fell for seven straight sessions. The Nasdaq fell 10.02% on the week.
  - The S&P 500 fell 8.61% on the week.
  - It is about 11% below its October high.
- Stress sources are unresolved: the Nvidia SEC probe, AI funding fears, a Fed in hiking mode with a possible 50bp surprise, and elevated implied correlation. Crowded positioning is concentrated in eight stocks that make up 35% of the S&P 500.
- The relief rally on Nov 18 failed within two days.
- The VIX rose from 16.6 to 40 in about 12 trading days. Vol-of-vol is high, and some investors are positioning for more turbulence.
- The window still has 22 trading days, including the Fed meeting.

**Caveat:** several of the sources above are secondary or aggregator sites with small inconsistencies (for example, closes of 35.89 vs "36", and intraday highs of 30.04 vs 32 vs 40.03). The Yahoo and CNBC quote data are the most reliable.

**1. Current status**
- The latest figure I found is **567 sites, as of 28 October 2026**. The breakdown is 165 religious sites, 289 buildings of historical and/or artistic interest, 43 museums, 33 monuments, 24 libraries, 8 archaeological sites and 5 archives. This comes from UNESCO's tracker page.
- The previous values were 560 on 23 September 2026 (per your question background; CFR also cites 560 at end of September 2026) and about 545 on 29 July (560 minus the 15 added in September).

- Strikes on 18–20 November 2026 damaged heritage sites, and none of this is in the UNESCO count yet. UNESCO condemned the 18 Nov attack inside the "Historic Centre of Odesa" World Heritage property. It said the strikes reportedly damaged several heritage buildings, including the Kalio Palace. UNESCO said it was ready to help Ukrainian authorities assess the damage.
- The Art Newspaper reports damage on 19–20 November to St Michael's Golden-Domed Monastery and St Volodymyr's Cathedral in Kyiv. Ukraine's Culture Ministry says 12 heritage sites in Odesa's historic centre were damaged, which it puts at 212 damaged heritage sites in Odesa in total.

The rate is now about 2.7 million rial, or roughly 270,000 toman. Check the Jan 1 baseline against Bonbast's own chart before relying on it.

**1. Current status (undecided; the resolution date is 39 days away)**
- **Nov 21, 2026:** The dollar fell to 270,000 tomans on Iran's parallel market on Saturday, from 272,900 on Friday, per Bonbast selling rates.
- **Nov 16, 2026:** the Bonbast archive showed a sell rate of 268,600 and a buy rate of 267,000.
- **Nov 18, 2026:** AlanChand showed a sell price of 2,685,000 rial, with a 24-hour range of 2,672,500 to 2,702,000.
- **Nov 22, 2026:** Arz Parz showed 268,250 toman.
- **Rough trend by date:**
  - Aug 22–24: about 195,000, then 200,050 tomans.
  - Sep 29: about 2.4–2.5 million rial, from two aggregators.
  - Oct 3: 267,100 sell.
  - Oct 22: 272,200.
  - Nov 21: about 270,000.
- The rate has been roughly flat at 265,000–273,000 for about seven weeks. That follows a rise of about 35% from late August to early October.
- **Inflation:** Consumer prices rose 88.7% year on year in the month ended Oct 22 (Statistical Center of Iran). Separately, the central bank put annual inflation at 83.8% in September.
- **Central bank intervention:** In early October the central bank said it would inject up to $2 billion into the FX market through state banks. This may help explain the plateau. I did not find confirmation of how much was actually injected.

**2. Resolution source (Bonbast)**
- Bonbast's home page showed sell 269,700 and buy 268,100 for USD at 19:36 UTC on Nov 21. The same page lists Tether at 272,300 toman.
- The question doesn't say whether "sell" or "buy" is used. The spread is about 1,600 toman, or 0.6%. The differences between aggregators are about the same size.

**3. Base rate and historical movement**
- **2018 (sanctions reimposed):** Bonbast showed 160,000 rial in Sept 2018. It was 75,000 in May 2018, so the rate more than doubled in about four months.
- **2022 (protest unrest):** 331,800 rial on Oct 3, up from 298,200 at the start of September. That is about 11% in a month.
- **Sept 2025:** Bonbast moved from about 950,000 rial in early September to about 1,085,000 on Sept 26. That is a rise of about 14% in a few weeks.
- **2026, based on the figures above:** about 1.35 million on Jan 1 and about 2.7 million now. That is a doubling, or a roughly 50% fall in the rial's value, in under 11 months. Counted on the dollar price, the rise since Jan 1 is about 100%, not "a third".
- **Pattern:** rises come in jumps around sanctions and war news, with plateaus or partial retracements on diplomatic hopes. Examples are the mid-September 2025 dip and the October 2026 plateau.
- **Rough size of moves:** a 39-day move of ±10–15% is common in this regime. That implies a range of roughly 235,000–310,000 toman, wider in the tails. This is my arithmetic from the historical moves above, not a published forecast.
- **Inflation pressure:** annual inflation near 85–90% points to a drift weaker of about 5–7% a month over time. The plateau suggests offsetting factors.

**4. Scheduled and likely events before Dec 31**
- **Escalation risk:** CBS reported on Nov 21 that the US and Israel are weighing a new assault that could launch within two to four days of an order. Trump said Iran doesn't want a deal acceptable to him.
- **Trump's timing:** a CBS live-blog headline says Trump warns the next move may not come until 2027. I did not verify the details.
- **Sanctions and blockade:** The US naval blockade has been in force since April 13, reimposed July 14, and extended to ship-to-ship transfers on Nov 18. Treasury sanctioned four Iranian oil-proceeds collectors on Nov 20–21. Expect more sanctions rounds.
- **Mediation:** Witkoff and Kushner met Qatari officials in Berlin on Nov 19. Qatari and Iranian officials also met that week.
- **Iran's stated position:** On Nov 9, Pezeshkian said Mojtaba Khamenei had ordered an end to the state of "neither war nor peace". Washington appears unwilling to accept Iran's seven demands.
- **Analysis view:** Al Jazeera (Nov 17) asks whether the conflict is becoming a "frozen conflict".
- **Not found:** I found no specific scheduled dates, such as a deadline, an OPEC or IAEA meeting, or Iranian budget or central bank decisions. Yalda and year-end are not known catalysts.

**5. Prediction markets and forecasters**
- I did not find Polymarket, Metaculus, or Kalshi markets, or analyst forecasts, for this rate.
- Trading Economics and Investing.com pages that came up show an official or non-market USD/IRR of about 1.91–1.94 million. That is a different series and not usable for this question.
- One official ICE transfer-rate page showed about 1.85 million rial on Oct 28.

**6. Strongest evidence on each side**

*Toward a higher dollar (weaker toman, above 270,000):*
- Inflation is about 85–90% a year, and the rate has tended to rise over the year.
- The blockade and sanctions are intensifying.
- A new US/Israeli strike is being weighed, and Trump says no deal is acceptable.
- Tether trades at a premium (272,300).
- The rate has repeatedly set new records, and the plateau is only seven weeks old.

*Toward a flat or lower dollar (at or below 270,000):*
- The rate has held in a 261,000–273,000 band since early October, despite continued sanctions.
- The central bank announced a $2 billion injection.
- Mediation is active, and Iran's supreme leader has authorized faster talks. Any ceasefire or sanctions-relief headline could pull the rate down sharply, as the June MoU did.
- Nov 21 saw a 1–2% pullback.

**Gaps:** I could not retrieve Bonbast's chart data for Jan 1 or for the June MoU period. I could not confirm the October peak. I could not confirm whether the question uses Bonbast's sell or buy rate.

## Web research
**Briefing: UK cabinet departures, 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Dec 2026**

**1. Current status (as of 22 Nov 2026)**
- I found no reports of any of the 18 listed cabinet ministers leaving after 1 Sep 2026. My searches were limited and returned nothing for Sept–Nov. I could not confirm a clean record.
- On current information the count is **0**. The question is undecided, leaning towards 0, with about 5.5 weeks left.
- Burnham became Labour leader on 17 July and PM on 20 July 2026. He was elected unopposed after receiving nominations from more than 90% of Labour MPs.
- The big churn came at government formation, before the window opens.
  - Reeves, Lammy, Darren Jones, Reed, Kyle, Kendall, Thomas-Symonds and Hermer were removed. Several others, including Hilary Benn, Jo Stevens and Baroness Chapman, also left government.
  - These changes are outside the window, which only counts departures after 1 Sep.
- Burnham has said he won't call an early general election. He plans to govern on Labour's existing manifesto.
- A discrepancy to note: one article is dated 26 Aug 2026 but describes the cabinet appointments as happening "on Monday". I could not reconcile this with the 20 July date. It doesn't change the analysis.

**2. Resolution source**
- The named source is https://members.parliament.uk/government/cabinet. I could not retrieve it.
- Wikipedia's "Burnham ministry" page was updated about 5 days ago. The snippet I saw lists only the July changes and shows no later cabinet departures.
- One wrinkle: the question uses "top 18 ranked cabinet members as of July 20". A reshuffle that moves someone between posts, rather than out of cabinet, may be ambiguous. The wording says "leave their positions".

**3. Base rate**
- I did not compute precise figures. The following is from memory and the sources above.
- Departures in the first 5 months of a new UK PM's government are usually low, because the PM has just picked loyal people.
- Examples of early departures:
  - Gavin Williamson left Sunak's cabinet about 2 weeks after Sunak took office in Oct 2022.
  - Several Starmer cabinet members left in the first 15 months, including Angela Rayner (Sept 2025), Louise Haigh (Nov 2024) and Tulip Siddiq (Treasury, Jan 2025). Siddiq was not in cabinet.
- Typical rate: roughly 0–2 cabinet exits in a given quarter outside crisis periods. Crises produce clusters, such as Brown in June 2009, Johnson in July 2022, and Starmer in May 2026.
- Context for this government: Streeting resigned from Starmer's cabinet on 14 May 2026 during the leadership crisis. The question table now lists him as Defence Secretary.

**4. Scheduled events before 1 Jan 2027**
- I found nothing scheduled, and my searches did not surface any pending autumn reshuffle or Budget date.
- Possible triggers:
  - An autumn Budget or fiscal statement. Healey is a new Chancellor.
  - Scandals or investigations.
  - Burnham reorganising departments. He has already merged the science department into Business.
  - Ministers leaving for other roles.
  - A mini-reshuffle to fill vacancies.
- Two Wikipedia-style facts bear on stability:
  - Louise Haigh, now First Secretary of State, has authority over the rest of the cabinet. She resigned from Starmer's cabinet in Nov 2024 over a past fraud conviction.
  - Lucy Powell is Deputy Leader and Education Secretary.
- Reported backlash over Burnham's appointment of Anas Sarwar as a peer and minister (Sarwar is stepping down as Scottish Labour leader) is not a cabinet departure. It could cause friction with Scottish ministers, including Douglas Alexander as Scotland Secretary.

**5. Markets and forecasters**
- I found no prediction-market or forecaster figures on this question. I did not find a Polymarket, Betfair or Metaculus market on cabinet departures.

**6. Evidence on each side**
- **For 0 departures (likely):**
  - The cabinet was formed only ~4 months ago from allies and a unity-style selection, and the last ministers who might rebel were removed in July.
  - No reported scandal or resignation in Sept–Nov that I could find.
  - A new PM with a large mandate (90%+ of MPs nominated him) has little pressure for a reshuffle in his first year.
  - Only about 5.5 weeks remain.
- **For 1 or more departures:**
  - Cabinet ministers have left at a high rate in recent UK governments, and the political environment has been volatile in 2026.
  - A first-year reshuffle or ad hoc scandal exit is possible. A cabinet of 18 over about 4 months has a non-trivial chance of at least one exit, perhaps 10–20% by my rough sense. That is not a sourced figure.
  - Ambiguity in how a role move or department change would be counted.
- **Gaps:** I could not check news from Sept–Nov in detail, and I could not check the live Parliament cabinet page. A direct check of both before forecasting would be worthwhile.

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: Will the US attack Oman before 2027?** (as of 2026-11-22)

**1. Current status: criteria look NOT MET on current information.**
- I found no report of a US strike on Omani territory, territorial waters, forces, vessels, or nationals.
- Trump has threatened Oman verbally twice.
  - On May 27, 2026 he said at a Cabinet meeting: "Oman will behave just like everybody else, or we'll have to blow 'em up."
  - On Aug 17, 2026, in a Fox News phone interview, he said: "If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the s--- out of them."
  - The Aug 17 threat came as the 60-day US-Iran deadline agreed in June expired. It was prompted by questions about Oman-Iran talks over the status of the strait.
- Congress and the State Department:
  - Sen. Kaine said he would introduce a resolution barring military action against Oman.
  - Kaine and Schiff introduced S.J.Res. in September 2026. I did not find its status.
  - On Nov 20, 2026, Secretary of State Rubio's National Day message said the US values its partnership with Oman and will keep working with it toward regional stability. This is conciliatory.
- Congressional Research Service, updated Nov 4, 2026:
  - US-Omani relations in the context of the Iran conflict are "uncertain."
  - Qatar, Turkey and Pakistan, not Oman, are now the lead interlocutors with Iran.
  - It also notes distrust of Oman among some Trump administration officials, while others see its role as potentially valuable.
  - Oman's sultan made a China visit (reported Nov 2) and Oman signed a currency swap with China (reported Nov 3).
- Backdrop: the war is in an escalating "no war, no peace" phase.
  - Iran increased military actions and its attempt to break the US naval blockade appeared imminent (Euronews, Nov 21).
  - At least three tankers were attacked in or near Hormuz on Nov 21.
  - On Nov 21 CBS reported that Trump said he is "not rushing" and could wait until 2027 to decide his next move.
  - Iran International, Nov 21, said Iran's tankers may try to run the blockade and Iran threatens Gulf oil facilities if fired on.

**Main accidental-attack pathway: the US blockade.**
- The US is firing on blockade-runners in the Gulf of Oman. This is where an accidental or ambiguous Omani-waters incident could arise.
  - On Nov 8, CENTCOM fired precision munitions at the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda. That was about 18 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan, UAE, which is not Omani waters.
  - Another strike hit the Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman on Oct 10.
  - CENTCOM says since July it has redirected 147 vessels and disabled five that refused.

## Web research
**Briefing: total US executions in 2026 (as of Nov 22, 2026)**

**1. Current status**
- **Count so far:** The count is 38 or 39, and I could not pin it down. Sources disagree.
  - AP reported on Nov 19 that Florida's execution of Thomas Overton brought the nation to 38 executions to date this year.
  - Reinaldo Dennes was then the second person executed in the United States on Thursday, Nov 19. DPIC's database lists his execution on November 19, 2026 in Texas. On AP's count that makes 39.
  - My own tally from the DPIC-style lists gives 38. Jamaal Howard (Oct 7) was the 30th. Then came Robertson (Oct 13), Reaves (Oct 20), three on Nov 5, one in Oklahoma on Nov 12, Overton and Dennes. Wikipedia's list showed a total of 37 when I retrieved it, probably before Dennes.
  - Whoever checks should read DPIC's execution page directly. The true figure is probably 38 or 39.
- **Failed attempt:** Christa Pike's Sept 30 execution failed in Tennessee and is not counted.
- **Remaining 2026 dates:** DPIC's upcoming-executions page (updated Nov 19) lists three:
  - Dec 1 Ricardo Gonzalez (FL), Dec 3 Nidal Malik Hasan (Military), Dec 10 Willie Seth Crain Jr. (FL).
- **Resolution status:** The final total is undecided. The floor is 38–39 and the ceiling is 41–42.

**2. Resolution source (DPIC)**
- The DPIC homepage (snapshot likely from before Nov 19) says 1693 men and women have been executed in the United States since the 1970s.
- The Texas Dennes entry is already in DPIC's database.
- The question says military executions count even if DPIC does not list them. Hasan would therefore count if carried out.

**3. Base rate**
- **2025:** Florida carried out a record 19 executions in 2025.
- **2026:** Florida is on 20, a new record, with two more executions planned in December.
- **2024:** There were 25 executions across the U.S.
- **2025 national total:** From memory, about 47, not verified in this search.
- **Warrant follow-through:** Executions scheduled in Florida have almost all proceeded this year. I saw one Florida stay (Mar 31) and one Georgia stay (Sept 16) in the Catholic Mobilizing list. Overall the outcome rate for warrants is high but not 100%.

**4. Scheduled events that could change the outcome**
- **Dec 1, Ricardo Gonzalez (FL, 6 p.m.):** He was convicted of killing a police officer in 1992. At resentencing four jurors voted to spare his life. I found no reported stay.
- **Dec 3, Nidal Hasan (Army firing squad, Fort Hood, 1 p.m. CT):**
  - Trump approved the sentence on Oct 2, and the Army set the date (Dec. 3, 2026).
  - Hasan could put them on hold — potentially for years — with a habeas corpus appeal in the civilian federal court system.
  - ABC (Nov 20) says it's unclear whether either will happen, meaning a habeas petition or a judge's delay.
  - This would be the first military execution in about 65 years, and the Army has to assemble a firing squad for the first time since 1945. It is the least certain of the three.
- **Dec 10, Willie Crain Jr. (FL, 6 p.m.):** He is 80 years old. The warrant was signed around Nov 10–11.
- **Other risks:**
  - Florida has faced controversy over altered lethal-injection drug logs (Wite-Out used to change expiration dates).
  - Texas had an emergency request over an expired lethal-injection drug, which was denied.
  - Dennes' execution took over an hour, which could prompt litigation.
- **New warrants:** I saw no other 2026 dates. DeSantis could sign another warrant for late December, but Florida warrants usually run about 30 days, so a new one would need to be signed soon. I did not find one.

**5. Markets and forecasters**
- I found no prediction-market or forecaster numbers for this question.
- DPI's Veterans Day piece (Nov 11) says the country is on pace to execute 11 veterans in 2026.

**6. Evidence on each side**
- **Higher end (41–42):**
  - Florida has carried out nearly all its warrants this year.
  - Both Florida cases are at advanced stages.
  - Hasan's date is fixed and the Army and the White House are committed to it.
- **Lower end (38–39):**
  - Hasan could be delayed by a habeas petition or a federal judge, since a first-ever modern firing-squad military execution is legally novel.
  - Last-minute stays are possible in Florida.
  - Drug and procedure problems (Pike's failure, Dennes' botched procedure, the expired-drug claims) could stall executions.
- **Most likely range, from the facts above:** The Florida pair probably adds 2, and Hasan is the swing case. That points to roughly 40–42 if the base is 38 or 39. The base-count discrepancy shifts every outcome by 1.

question.title: What will be the total spending by all Senate candidates in the 2026 US election cycle?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: total spending by all Senate candidates, 2026 cycle (FEC "Spending: by the numbers")**

**1. Current status (as of Nov 22, 2026)**
- No final figure exists yet, so the question is undecided. The result is a cumulative FEC total that is still rising.
- The Post-General report is due Dec 3, 2026. It covers activity from the close of the last reporting period through November 23. Year-end reports are due in January 2027.
- Latest data points on Senate candidate disbursements:
  - FEC, Jan 1, 2025 to Mar 31, 2026: 291 Senate candidates reported disbursements of $400.8 million.
  - FEC, through Jun 30, 2026: 315 Senate candidates reported disbursements of $614.2 million.
  - Question background, mid-August 2026: $666.3M.
  - USAFacts, FEC data downloaded Oct 28, 2026: Candidates have spent a total of $1.18 billion on 2026 Senate races. The figure is counted since Jan 2025. It is the best recent proxy and sits below the 2024 figure of $1.687B.
- Other trackers use narrower definitions and are not comparable:
  - VoteLog, Nov 10: $900,575,463 spent by the campaigns (cycle-to-date) across the 35 general-election races only. This excludes candidates who lost primaries.
  - Dave Manuel's tracker, Nov 10: Candidate spending includes candidates who lost their primaries. It says Senate campaigns are counted over the full six-year cycle. It shows Texas candidates at $192M and Ohio at $84.8M.
- OpenSecrets projects about $11.9B total federal spending. It projects $3.7 billion from House and Senate candidates and $3.9 billion from outside groups. I found no Senate-only candidate figure from OpenSecrets.
- Spending was heavily concentrated in a few races. Top Senate spenders as of Oct 28 (USAFacts):
  - Talarico (TX): $136.4M
  - Ossoff (GA): $105.8M
  - Sherrod Brown (OH): $64.0M
  - El-Sayed (MI): $51.1M
  - Cooper (NC): $40.5M
- Texas is the highest-spending state, at $182 million in the USAFacts count.

**2. Resolution source**
- The FEC "Spending: by the numbers" page is JavaScript-rendered. I could not retrieve its current Senate 2026 figure.
- One scan noted that the tool "includes data up to and including the most recent report". Its value therefore lags actual spending and updates as reports are processed.
- The last published value I can verify is the mid-August $666.3M quoted in the question. That figure may be stale or reflect a processing lag. I could not confirm the current number.

**3. Base rate**
- Past final totals from the FEC tool:
  - 2020: $2.008B
  - 2022: $1.708B
  - 2024: $1.687B
- For comparison, the FEC reported that 2024 House and Senate candidates spent $1.8 billion between January 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024. That is a combined figure.
- 2026 combined House and Senate candidate spending was $2.0B through Jun 30, 2026. This is well ahead of the 2024 pace.
- 2026 Senate disbursements rose from $400.8M (Mar 31) to $614.2M (Jun 30), roughly +$213M in one quarter. Mid-August stood at $666M. Per USAFacts, the Oct 28 figure was $1.18B.
- Spending accelerates sharply before the election. I did not find the pre-election vs final ratio for past cycles.

**4. Scheduled events before resolution**
- Pre-General report: covers through about Oct 14. Its data is likely already in the Oct 28 USAFacts download.
- 24/48-hour reports and processing continue.
- Post-General report due Dec 3, 2026.
- Year-End report due Jan 31, 2027, which is after the question's Dec 31 window.
- Georgia Senate runoff: I did not check whether one is occurring in 2026. A runoff would add spending.
- The FEC tool may not show Post-General data until late December or later.

**5. Forecasters and markets**
- I found no prediction markets or forecaster numbers on this specific question.
- The only item I found is an automated scan summary on the Metaculus question. It offers no point estimate.

**6. Evidence on each side**
- Toward a higher total, above about $1.7B:
  - Record overall midterm spending.
  - Texas alone was at $192M of candidate spending by Nov 10 in one tracker.
  - Post-Oct 28 spending in the final week, plus post-election disbursements, is still to be added.
  - Combined candidate spending (House and Senate) is far ahead of 2024.
- Toward a lower total, below about $1.7B:
  - The USAFacts figure of $1.18B on Oct 28 is about $0.5B below the 2024 final.
  - VoteLog's $0.90B campaign figure on Nov 10 covers only general-election candidates.
  - Much of the 2026 money is outside spending, which does not count as candidate spending.
  - The FEC tool lags reports.
- A plausible central range, in my judgment only, is $1.3B to $1.6B once final reports are in. The uncertainty is large because the definitions differ. I could not verify what the FEC tool counts, for example transfers or double-counted committee-to-committee flows. The FEC tool's totals for past cycles have been higher than some trackers' figures.

  - The assumed cash drawdown to $850B from $984B at Sep 30 reduces borrowing needs.

- The Dec 31, 2025 figure ($38.51T) comes from a secondary site, but it agrees with USAFacts's "over $38.5T."

question.title: Who will win the 2026 World Chess Championship?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: 2026 World Chess Championship (Gukesh vs Sindarov)**

**1. Current status (as of 22 Nov 2026)**
- The criteria are **undecided**. No classical games have been played. One source dated 4 days ago shows 0 of 14 classical games played.
- The question's background says Nov 25–Dec 15, but the schedule has changed. ChessBase says the match was first announced for 25 Nov–15 Dec and that in August, FIDE moved it forward to 22 November to 12 December.
- Another source says the regulations were approved by the FIDE Council on 23 August 2026 and published on 28 August. Under them, Game 1 is on 24 Nov and Game 14 on 11 Dec. The opening ceremony and colour draw are on 22 Nov, and tiebreaks, if needed, are on 12 Dec.
- The match is still well before 31 Dec, so the postponement-annulment clause looks unlikely to apply. I found no reports of a forfeit threat, illness or venue problems.
- The venue is Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny, Geneva. Games start at 15:00 Geneva time.
- Format: 14 classical games, and first to 7½ wins. Tiebreaks are rapid (10+5), then blitz (3+2), then sudden-death games, until one is decisive.
- Colours for Game 1 are drawn at the opening ceremony on 22 Nov. I did not find the result of that draw.
- Ratings (Nov 2026 list):
  - Gukesh is world No. 26 with a rating of 2710, 72 Elo points behind Sindarov. Sindarov is world No. 4 at 2782.
  - Gukesh lost 84 rating points from his October 2024 peak of 2794.
- Sindarov's qualification: he won the 2025 World Cup. He then won the 2026 Candidates (28 Mar–16 Apr, Cyprus) with 10 points of 14. He won with a round to spare and set a Candidates points record.

**2. Resolution source**
- FIDE (fide.com/news) is the named source. It has no result yet because the match has not started.
- FIDE's calendar and press pages still list the match as 25 Nov–15 Dec, while newer secondary sources say 24 Nov–12 Dec. I could not open FIDE's own pages to confirm which is current.

**3. Base rate**
- I did not find a sourced statistic on how often the champion or the higher-rated player wins a title match. The points below are from my own knowledge and not from the searches.
- Classical title matches are usually close. The 2024 match (Gukesh vs Ding) went to Game 14 and was decided 7½–6½. The 2018 Carlsen–Caruana match was 12 draws, then Carlsen won the rapid tiebreak.
- Higher-rated challengers have sometimes lost. Ding, who was rated well below the other top players, nearly beat Gukesh in 2024. One commentator noted that Ding Liren almost beat Gukesh in the last World Championship after looking like a shell of his former self.
- One simulation site gives 12.2% of matches going to tiebreaks.
- Head-to-head: Sindarov leads 2-0 in classical games with one draw. Those were wins at the 2018 Moscow Open (when they were children) and the 2022 Sharjah Masters. The 2026 Tata Steel game was drawn.

**4. Events before resolution**
- 22 Nov: opening ceremony and colour draw at the Palais des Nations.
- 24 Nov: Game 1. Games 1–3 run 24–26 Nov, with a rest day on 27 Nov. The calendar then continues with rest days roughly every three games.
- 11 Dec: Game 14, the last scheduled classical game.
- 12 Dec: tiebreaks and closing ceremony, if the score is 7–7.
- The match can end early once someone reaches 7½, which could be as soon as Game 8.

**5. Markets and forecasters**
- Polymarket (page about 15 days old): Sindarov 77%, Gukesh 24%. Volume is only about $82K per side, so it is thin. The page's market end date is Jun 30, 2027.
- Earlier Polymarket snapshots: 75% for Sindarov around mid-May, and another snapshot that showed 63%. A pawnalyze snapshot (about 8 weeks old) showed Gukesh 25¢/27¢ and Sindarov 74¢/76¢.
- Bookmaker bet365 (as of 27 Sept): Gukesh 2/1, Sindarov 4/11, about 31% vs 69% after removing the margin.
- Ratings-only simulation (pawnalyze): Gukesh 14.9%, and Sindarov wins about 85 in 100 matches. The model uses only ratings. Its own site notes that markets give Gukesh about twice the model's chance.
- Experts: Carlsen called Sindarov "a pretty significant favorite" (Sept 2026). Nakamura suggested odds of roughly 75-25 for Sindarov.

**6. Evidence on each side**
- **For Sindarov:**
  - He has a 72-point rating edge and recent results: the 2025 World Cup, an unbeaten 2026 Candidates, and second place at Tata Steel in Jan 2026 without a loss.
  - A pawnalyze snippet notes that Sindarov won both games at Grand Chess Tour Poland 2026.
  - Gukesh has been criticised for poor form in both classical and faster time controls. He has fallen out of the top 10 (No. 26).
  - Carlsen, Nakamura, bookmakers and the markets all favour Sindarov.
- **For Gukesh:**
  - He has already won a title match, in a pressure format, while this is Sindarov's first.
  - The match is short, 14 games, and draw-heavy. Preparation and nerves can outweigh recent form.
  - Ding's near-comeback in 2024 shows form is a weak predictor of match outcomes.
  - Sindarov's classical head-to-head lead is only three games, two of them from childhood and teen years.
  - A tied match goes to rapid and blitz tiebreaks, where the outcome is closer to a coin flip. Sindarov's record there looks strong, though: he won both blitz games against Gukesh (Gukesh won their only rapid game).
  - Some bettors appear to be pricing Gukesh well above the ratings-model figure. I did not find evidence of an unpublished Gukesh recovery in form.

**Not found:** the colour-draw result, live match results, or any FIDE statement confirming the final dates.
